title: Text That Uses Every Letter
statement:
You get a string text made of lowercase English letters only, with no spaces.

Return true if every one of the 26 letters from a to z appears in text at least once, and false otherwise.

examples.why: A known pangram: each of the 26 letters shows up, some of them more than once.
Order and repeats do not matter, only which letters appear.

constraints: text contains only lowercase English letters
hints: You only need to know which letters appeared, not how many times or where.
Put the letters in a set and check its size. A string with fewer than 26 characters can never pass.
Without a set: keep a 26-bit number and set bit (c − 'a') for each letter. The text passes when the number equals 2²⁶ − 1.

explain.intuition:
The question is about the set of distinct letters, so build that set. The text uses every letter exactly when the set has 26 members, since only lowercase letters can appear.

A 26-bit integer is a compact set: bit i means "letter i seen". Setting a bit twice changes nothing, which handles repeats for free. It is the same trick as packing feature flags into one number.
pitfalls: Checking text.length ≥ 26 instead of the number of different letters. Repeats can fill the length without covering the alphabet.
Off-by-one in the full mask: 1 << 26 alone is a single bit, the full mask is (1 << 26) − 1.
Counting how many letters occur at least twice, or similar, instead of simply which letters occur.

solutions.title: Set of letters
solutions.idea: Collect the distinct letters and check that there are 26.

solutions.title: 26-bit mask
solutions.idea: Set one bit per letter seen and compare with the mask that has all 26 bits on. Stop early once it is full.

followups: The text is mixed case with spaces and punctuation. What changes, and what should count as a letter?
Return the letters that are missing, in alphabetical order.
lcTitle: Check if the Sentence Is Pangram
